title: New Orleans pianists and their styles
summary: He names the old-time pianists he knew, Steve Lewis, Fate Marable, Udell Wilson, and the great Cooney Vaughn of Hattiesburg.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And you remember the earliest piano players that you heard in New Orleans? Did you hear any of the players in the district, for instance?
Well, practically I knew practically all the old timers around. Steve Lewis. Yeah. Walter Pigeon, Fats Pigeon, and Red Caillou, Udell Wilson.
Yeah.
And Poiré Nolan, Little Willie, Little Dookie, Little Sammy.
Little Sammy. Were some of those fellows mostly blues players, or did they play ragtime? Well, they played ragtime. Jazz, jazz piano.
All sorts. All sorts. Did you hear Manuel Moneta?
Do you remember him?
I didn't ever remember him in person.
He's been teaching mostly across the river, so hasn't played much in late years. Did all of the bands use piano mostly, or some of the bands? Not at that time.
I know, didn't. Just a few bands used piano. Well, Pierone, Steve Lewis was playing with him. Yeah. Fate Marble, he was a piano player. Yeah. He had a band, he had the band on the boat.
Yeah.
Stimma Capital.
What kind of a pianist was Fate? He was a good pianist. He was nice at the time.
And Udell, at the time, he was about one of the best around in New Orleans, Udell, I think his home was in Kansas City.
Yeah, I think, I think I heard that too. What does Steve Lewis' style like? I know it's hard to explain just by words, but still.
He was a good piano player too. He played kind of on the order of Jelly Roll. Jelly Roll Mug.
Did you hear Jelly Roll any place in your travels?
Oh yeah, I heard him in Chicago. In Chicago, yeah.
I knew him, got to hear him. He was wonderful I thought too. Anything else about those early pianists that you can remember?

Well there were some great piano players down through and some of the greatest, one of the greatest piano players ever I looked at was Cooney Vons. He was from Hattiesburg, Mississippi. And they had another one there they called Blind Jug. He was a good. And also another one they called Gus Permer. He was great. Yeah.
